claims.statement: A thread’s durable sandbox binding is `sandbox_id` in thread metadata, while `SANDBOX_BACKENDS` is a worker-local map of stable per-thread proxies; metadata lookup prefers inline run metadata, falls back to the live thread, and returns no metadata on lookup failure.

`SandboxBackendProxy` is an async-only stable handle whose target can be replaced; missing targets reconnect through a registered callback or metadata ID, and a lock plus shared startup task ensures concurrent callers use one reconnect.
The proxy subclasses `BaseSandbox` so filesystem tooling retains capture-at-source behavior, and its offload method delegates when supported or reports an ordinary-execution fallback.

`create_sandbox` selects a lazily imported provider factory from `SANDBOX_TYPE`; supported values are langsmith, daytona, modal, runloop, e2b, and local, with langsmith receiving creation overrides and synchronous factories offloaded to threads.
New thread sandboxes use an environment’s ready snapshot when available or the admin base snapshot otherwise, and carry environment resource settings and create parameters into provisioning.
LangSmith startup validation checks configured numeric sizing and retention values, rejects negative retention TTLs, and validates extra create JSON before the first sandbox creation.

LangSmith command retries are limited to `SandboxRetryableConnectionError`, which represents a rejected WebSocket upgrade before the command frame was sent; retries are bounded and use exponential jittered backoff.

`ensure_sandbox_for_thread` reuses a cached backend, reconnects through a metadata ID, or creates a new box; thread dispatch interruption is relied upon to avoid concurrent provisioning without a cross-process sentinel.
Sandbox initialization writes metadata only after creation and initialization, then publishes the backend last; failures before those steps do not expose a new backend through the thread proxy.

A deleted sandbox (`SandboxGoneError`) is always replaced, whereas an unreachable sandbox is not replaced by default because it may recover and may contain the only uncommitted working tree; a chosen replacement failure is surfaced as `SandboxUnreachableError`.
Only reviewer calls allow replacement of an unreachable sandbox because review repository preparation re-derives the checkout each run and reviewer threads persist per PR across pushes.

For LangSmith sandboxes, GitHub authentication is injected by proxy rules as a Bearer header for `api.github.com` and Basic authentication for GitHub web hosts, while the sandbox receives only a placeholder `GH_TOKEN`.
LangSmith proxy configuration preserves custom base rules, retries transient PATCH errors, and when a configuration PATCH reports the sandbox is not ready, best-effort starts it before retrying.

Proxy token records keep expiry, repository scope, permission scope, and base configuration per thread; before-model middleware refreshes LangSmith tokens within five minutes of known expiry or after 50 minutes when expiry is unknown.

`recreate_sandbox_for_thread` and LangSmith-only `reset_sandbox_for_thread` preserve the old sandbox, persist a distinct new ID before replacing the cached proxy target, and leave the old target in place when metadata persistence fails.

Desktop runs bypass the remote thread-sandbox lifecycle and use a local backend only for an allowlisted project or desktop-created worktree; desktop artifact routes keep internal files outside the project.
The local provider runs without isolation, scopes global Git configuration to `.gitconfig-sandbox`, and omits model and provider API keys from the child environment.
Sandbox repository paths are portable: the resolver tries provider work directories, shell paths, and provider or shell home paths, verifies writability, and caches the selected directory.

Reviewer repository preparation force-checks out and verifies the requested PR head, while reviewer skill directories are extracted from a trusted base reference outside the PR checkout rather than from PR-head content.

Environment refreshes run scripts on throwaway builder sandboxes: full refreshes start from the base snapshot and run setup then update, while update refreshes start from the ready snapshot and run only the update script; failed refreshes leave the prior snapshot available.
When an environment snapshot is stale, a newly created thread sandbox runs its update script before the first model call without making update failure fatal, then triggers a due background refresh.

Environment snapshot capture records a new immutable snapshot ID only after capture succeeds and deletes the superseded snapshot only after the record points to the new ID, preserving a prior ready snapshot on capture failure.

The LangSmith provider deliberately exposes no sandbox deletion operation because durable metadata lookup can fail open; sandbox retention and reclamation are configured at creation and handled by the platform.
`sandbox_reset` is an admin-gated tool that requires the current run's thread ID and returns either an error or the old and new sandbox IDs after calling the lifecycle reset operation.
Both normal and reviewer agents install the before-model GitHub proxy-refresh middleware.
